subject: keep getting "cholesky_decompose: Cholesky decomposition of m failed"

messages.author: e74863d19d180366
messages.subject: keep getting "cholesky_decompose: Cholesky decomposition of m failed"
parts:
Hello guys I am new to rstan and currently using it for stochastic mortality modelling. There is a covariance matrix in my model which I defined as cov_matrix[3] v in the parameters block. However I kept getting this "cholesky_decompose: Cholesky decomposition of m failed" error message as there is a multi-variate random walk in my model. The prior for this covariance matrix is Jeffery. I dont quite understand why the decompose failed as there is constraints for v? My code is as follows

data{

int<lower=0> m;

int<lower=0> n;

int dtx[m,n];

real etx[m,n];

real mtx[m,n];

real<lower=0> a_gamma;

real<lower=0> b_gamma;

int<lower=0> C;

vector[n] beta2v;

vector[n] beta3v;

real g;

}

parameters{

vector[m] kappa_1;

vector[m] kappa_2;

vector[m] kappa_3;

vector[C] gamma_par;

real<lower=-1,upper=1> alpha_gamma;

real<lower=0> sigma_gamma;

vector[3] mu;

cov_matrix[3] v;

}

transformed parameters{

matrix[3,3] chol_v;

chol_v <- cholesky_decompose(v);

}

model{

//define variables

matrix[m,n] mhat;

matrix[m,2] kappa_12;

matrix[m,3] kappa_par;

//matrix[3,3] chol_v;


kappa_12 <- append_col(kappa_1,kappa_2);

kappa_par <- append_col(kappa_12,kappa_3);

//chol_v <- cholesky_decompose(v);

//kappa_par[1]' ~ multi_normal_cholesky(mu,chol_v);

for(i in 2:m)

kappa_par[i]'-kappa_par[i-1]'~ multi_normal_cholesky(mu,chol_v);


//kappa_par[i]'-kappa_par[i-1]' ~ multi_normal(mu,v);


increment_log_prob(-2*log(determinant(v)));


square(sigma_gamma) ~ inv_gamma(a_gamma,b_gamma);

increment_log_prob(log(fabs(2*sigma_gamma)));

increment_log_prob(g*log(1-pow(alpha_gamma,2)));


gamma_par[1] ~ normal(0,sigma_gamma/sqrt(1-pow(alpha_gamma,2)));

for(c in 2:C)

gamma_par[c] ~ normal(alpha_gamma*gamma_par[c-1],sigma_gamma);


for(i in 1:m)

for(j in 1:n)

mhat[i,j] <- log(1+exp(kappa_1[i]+kappa_2[i]*beta2v[j]+kappa_3[i]*beta3v[j]+gamma_par[n+i-j]));


for(i in 1:m)

for(j in 1:n)

dtx[i,j] ~ poisson(etx[i,j]*mhat[i,j]);

}

Thanks a million

Liang

parts:
On Thursday, March 10, 2016 at 9:48:01 AM UTC-5, Liang Chen wrote:
Hello guys I am new to rstan and currently using it for stochastic mortality modelling. There is a covariance matrix in my model which I defined as cov_matrix[3] v in the parameters block. However I kept getting this "cholesky_decompose: Cholesky decomposition of m failed" error message as there is a multi-variate random walk in my model. The prior for this covariance matrix is Jeffery. I dont quite understand why the decompose failed as there is constraints for v? My code is as follows

It is better to declare chol_v as a parameter

parameters {
  ...
  cholesky_factor_cov[3] chol_v;
}

and then you don't have to deal with the numerical difficulties of doing the Cholesky decomposition when it gets nearly singular.

Ben

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: keep getting "cholesky_decompose: Cholesky decomposition of m failed"
parts:
On Thursday, March 10, 2016 at 10:21:08 AM UTC-5, Liang Chen wrote:

That makes sense thank you. So should I define the co-variance matrix v in the transformed parameters, as I am giving a Jeffery prior for v in the model, "increment_log_prob(-2*log(determinant(v)));”

Well,

det(v) = det(chol_v * chol_v') = det(chol_v) * det(chol_v') = det(chol_v)^2

so

increment_log_prob(-2 * log(determinant(v)));

becomes

increment_log_prob(-4 * sum(log(diag_vector(chol_v))));

But in case Andy is reading this, I'm not saying Jeffreys' prior makes the most sense here. I'm just saying you don't need v to evaluate it.

Ben
